curriculum.title: The First-Day and Weekly Practice Question

core.big_idea: Weekly first-day observance is a framework conclusion drawn from apostolic practice rather than a verse that states the frequency as a universal command.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate context; select age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Apostolic churches: The Lord's Supper within the Church, Worship, and Mission cycle

claims.statement: Acts 20:7 describes disciples gathering on the first day of the week to break bread.
1 Corinthians 16:1-2 describes a first-day-of-the-week collection practice in Corinth.
Weekly first-day observance is a framework conclusion drawn from apostolic practice rather than a verse that states the frequency as a universal command.
claims.interpretive_hinge: The framework reads recurring first-day apostolic practice together with the purpose and institution of the Supper as a normative weekly pattern, while acknowledging that neither cited verse states a universal frequency command in those exact words.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present this framework conclusion as an explicit biblical command or quotation.

core.interpretation_skill: Evaluate sources and arguments; identify assumptions; compare credible positions; state uncertainty precisely

learning.foundation_objective: Analyse the relevant text and explain the case that weekly first-day observance is a framework conclusion drawn from apostolic practice rather than a verse that states the frequency as a universal command.
learning.extension_objective: Test the claim against context, genre, canonical synthesis, credible alternatives, and the limits of the available evidence.
know: The principal passage is Acts 20:7; 1 Corinthians 16:1-2.
Weekly first-day observance is a framework conclusion drawn from apostolic practice rather than a verse that states the frequency as a universal command.
The lesson belongs in Apostolic churches.
understand: Direct observation must remain distinct from interpretation, synthesis, framework position, and application.
practise: Retell or analyse the passage using evidence from the text.
Name one faithful response without claiming more than the passage supports.
become: A learner who responds to Scripture with trust, wisdom, worship, service, repentance, or love as appropriate.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage.
Student can support the big idea with evidence.
Student can distinguish observation from interpretation or application.
